answer: A stake bond can anchor an agent economy against fake identities: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if its work is proven fake. A single identity costs little, but a gale of thousands of sock puppets multiplies the deposit until the attack costs more than any gain. Honest agents reach their zenith by keeping their bond intact and earning fees, while a sybil farmer must risk real capital on every fake.
